title: A revert merged with its tree already proven lifts red main, so merges resume without a full run of the old broken tree
why: Owner ruling own-823-b-revert-merge-lifts-red (page item 823, option b, 15:04 CST Nov 14, no note); the owner chose a widening knowingly; ruling own-745-b-resume-at-revert (owner 13:20 CST Nov 13) goes live. Today (the lane merge-flow-after-anthropic's probe, relayed, unchecked by triage): after a revert merges, its push run is skipped (the tree is already proven), and the red-main check reads the newest run that ran the tests, so main stays red until a full run is dispatched or `--base-red-ok` is used (own-812-a-judge-suite-runs). The refusal text also says `gh run rerun <id> --failed`, which re-tests the old broken commit (the lane files that wording as a debt in PR #3384, whichever way the owner picked). GRANT SCOPE: a revert whose tree is already proven only; a revert that does not fix the failure reads clear until the next full run (the cost the owner accepted). Any other merge onto red main stays refused. First act of a lane: read the check and the ruling records, write the red tests first: a revert merge with a proven tree lifts red; a non-revert merge onto red main is still refused; a revert whose tree is not proven is still refused; the check reads unknown when the run cannot be read, never clear. A guard verdict moves from refuse to pass: round 3 and the net-value test apply. Kin: merge-flow-after-anthropic, git-red-main-reverts (root rule). LANE STARTED 15:11 CST Nov 14 (coordinator's message headed 15:09; started 15:09 CST): lane session_013NEJL1bon7mMqXTg7ztbFj. MERGED 22:05:19 CST Nov 14 (GitHub REST read by triage: merged true, merged_at 04:05:19Z, head fc55c3ad7211; the PR body names this step and owner ruling own-823-b-revert-merge-lifts-red; coordinator 22:07: merge commit 8ebcdb6001a0 by REST and ls-remote, run 43671603171 success; relayed, triage read no diff). Per the PR body: a revert merged with its tree proven lifts red main; still refused: a non-revert merge, an unproven revert, a re-land, a red schedule or cancelled run beside the blamed red, a first red with no breaking merge named, any failed read. Accepted cost (owner): a revert that does not fix the failure reads clear until the next full run. Notes PR for #3427 started by its lane.
